title: King Charles gets drenched in Antigua rainstorm as Camilla gets only umbrella
summary: King Charles flung up his hands in despair as he was caught in a tropical rainstorm in Antigua, while his wife Queen Camilla strolled off with the only available umbrella.

image.caption: King Charles and Queen Camilla are pictured Sunday in the Sir Vivian Richards Stadium in St John’s, Antigua and Barbuda. They attended as part of a week-long autumn tour of Caribbean nations, including attendance at the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting. (Isabel Infantes/Pool/Reuters)

blocks.text: King Charles flung up his hands in despair as he was caught in a tropical rainstorm in Antigua, while his wife Queen Camilla strolled off with the only available umbrella.
The monarch was eventually given an umbrella at an Independence Day parade
The couple's Caribbean tour has been dominated by the debate over Britain's role in the slave trade, but it was the sight of the soaked monarch which made headlines on Sunday.

As the rain hammered down on Charles, 77, he was seen gesturing and turning round to try to attract the attention of someone who might help, while Camilla was shielded from the downpour. Locals taking part in the Antigua and Barbuda Independence Day parade did not flinch as they were lashed by the storm.
Charles was eventually given an umbrella and was seen joking about his experience with Prime Minister Gaston Browne.
King Charles gets soaked in Antigua as Camilla gets only umbrella
"I think I'm about to grow watercress on my suit," he said in a video posted on the Royal Family's Instagram account.
It is not the first time the frustration of the famously short-fused Charles has been captured in public.
Not long after he became king in 2022, in an incident which went viral on social media, he reacted grumpily when a pen leaked ink onto his hand at an event in Northern Ireland.
"Oh God, I hate this," he cursed.

blocks.text: "I can't bear this bloody thing … every stinking time," he continued.
He has since made fun of himself, quipping at a subsequent event, "I'm hoping that my pen is going to work. It doesn't usually."

He is due to make a speech to Commonwealth leaders on Tuesday. Since becoming king, he has expressed sorrow for the suffering caused by slavery without crossing a line that Britain has long resisted: an apology.

King Charles shelters from the rain under an umbrella on Sunday as he inspects the troops during the country’s annual Independence Day parade at the Sir Vivian Richards Stadium in Saint George, Antigua and Barbuda. (Aaron Chown/Pool/Reuters)
